{{Use shortened footnotes|date=May 2021}}
In [[mathematics]], especially [[functional analysis]], a '''Fréchet algebra''', named after [[Maurice René Fréchet]], is an [[associative algebra]] <math>A</math> over the [[real number|real]] or [[complex number|complex]] numbers that at the same time is also a ([[locally convex]]) [[Fréchet space]]. The multiplication operation <math>(a,b) \mapsto a*b</math> for <math>a,b \in A</math> is required to be jointly [[continuous function (topology)#Continuous functions between metric spaces|continuous]].
If <math>\{\| \cdot \|_n \}_{n=0}^\infty</math> is an [[increasing]] family{{efn|An increasing family means that for each <math>a \in A,</math>
:<math>\|a\|_0 \leq \|a\|_1 \leq \cdots \leq \| a \|_n \leq \cdots</math>.}} of [[semi-norms|seminorms]] for
the [[locally convex topological vector space|topology]] of <math>A</math>, the joint continuity of multiplication is equivalent to there being a constant <math>C_n >0</math> and integer <math>m \ge n</math> for each <math>n</math> such that <math>\left\| a b \right\|_n \leq C_n \left\| a \right\|_m \left\|b \right\|_m</math> for all <math> a, b \in A</math>.{{efn|Joint continuity of multiplication means that for every [[absolutely convex set|absolutely convex]] [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighborhood]] <math>V</math> of zero, there is an absolutely convex neighborhood <math>U</math> of zero for which <math>U^2 \subseteq V,</math> from which the seminorm inequality follows. Conversely,
::<math>\begin{align}
 &{} \| a_k b_k -a b \|_n \\
 &= \| a_k b_k - a b_k + a b_k - ab \|_n \\
 &\leq \| a_k b_k - a b_k \|_n + \| a b_k - ab \|_n \\
 &\leq C_n \biggl( \| a_k - a \|_m \|b_k\|_m  + \| a\|_m\| b_k - b \|_m \biggr) \\
 &\leq C_n \biggl( \| a_k - a \|_m \|b\|_m + \| a_k -a\|_m \|b_k - b\|_m + \| a\|_m\| b_k - b \|_m \biggr).
\end{align}</math>}} Fréchet algebras are also called ''B''<sub>0</sub>-algebras.{{sfnm|1a1=Mitiagin|1a2=Rolewicz|1a3=Żelazko|1y=1962|2a1=Żelazko|2y=2001}}

A Fréchet algebra is '''<math>m</math>-convex''' if [[there exists]] such a family of semi-norms for which <math>m=n</math>. In that case, by rescaling the seminorms, we may also take <math>C_n = 1</math> for each <math>n</math> and the seminorms are said to be '''submultiplicative''': <math>\| a b \|_n \leq \| a \|_n \| b \|_n</math> for all <math>a, b \in A.</math>{{efn|In other words, an <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebra is a [[topological algebra]], in which the topology is given by a countable family of submultiplicative seminorms: <math>p(fg) \le p(f) p(g),</math> and the algebra is complete.}} <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebras may also be called Fréchet algebras.<ref>{{harvnb|Husain|1991}}; {{harvnb|Żelazko|2001}}.</ref>

A Fréchet algebra may or [[associative algebra#Non-unital algebras|may not]] have an [[identity element|identity]] element <math>1_A </math>. If <math>A</math> is [[unital algebra|unital]], we do not require that <math>\|1_A\|_n=1,</math> as is often done for [[Banach algebra]]s.

==Properties==
* '''Continuity of multiplication.''' Multiplication is '''separately continuous''' if <math>a_k b \to ab</math> and <math>ba_k \to ba</math> for every <math>a, b \in A</math> and sequence <math>a_k \to a</math> converging in the Fréchet topology of <math>A</math>. Multiplication is '''jointly continuous''' if <math>a_k \to a</math> and <math>b_k \to b</math> imply <math>a_k b_k \to ab</math>. Joint continuity of multiplication is part of the definition of a Fréchet algebra. For a Fréchet space with an algebra structure, if the multiplication is separately continuous, then it is automatically jointly continuous.<ref>{{harvnb|Waelbroeck|1971|loc=Chapter VII, Proposition 1}}; {{harvnb|Palmer|1994|loc=<math>\S</math> 2.9}}.</ref>
* '''Group of invertible elements.''' If <math>invA</math> is the set of [[invertible element]]s of <math>A</math>, then the inverse map <math display="block">\begin{cases} invA \to invA \\ u \mapsto u^{-1} \end{cases}</math> is [[continuous function#Continuous functions between metric spaces|continuous]] if and only if <math>invA</math> is a [[G delta|<math>G_\delta</math> set]].{{sfn|Waelbroeck|1971|loc=Chapter VII, Proposition 2}} Unlike for [[Banach algebra#Properties|Banach algebras]], <math>inv A</math> may not be an [[open set]]. If <math>inv A</math> is open, then <math>A</math> is called a '''<math>Q</math>-algebra'''. (If <math>A</math> happens to be [[associative algebra#Non-unital algebras|non-unital]], then we may adjoin a [[identity element|unit]] to <math>A</math>{{efn|If <math>A</math> is an algebra over a field <math>k</math>, the '''unitization''' <math>A^+</math> of <math>A</math> is the direct sum <math>A \oplus k 1</math>, with multiplication defined as <math>(a+ \mu 1)(b + \lambda 1) = ab + \mu b + \lambda a + \mu \lambda 1.</math>}} and work with <math>inv A^+</math>, or the set of quasi invertibles{{efn|If <math>a \in A</math>, then <math>b \in A</math> is a '''quasi-inverse''' for <math>a</math> if <math>a + b -ab = 0</math>.}} may take the place of <math>inv A</math>.)
* '''Conditions for <math>m</math>-convexity.''' A Fréchet algebra is <math>m</math>-convex if and only if [[for every]], if and only if [[there exists|for one]], increasing family <math>\{ \| \cdot \|_n \}_{n=0}^\infty</math> of seminorms which topologize <math>A</math>, for each <math>m \in \N</math> there exists <math> p \geq m </math> and <math>C_m>0</math> such that <math display="block"> \| a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n \|_m \leq C_m^n \| a_1 \|_p \| a_2 \|_p \cdots \| a_n \|_p,</math> for all <math>a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \in A</math> and <math>n \in \N</math>.{{sfn|Mitiagin|Rolewicz|Żelazko|1962|loc=Lemma 1.2}} A [[commutative ring|commutative]] Fréchet <math>Q</math>-algebra is <math>m</math>-convex,{{sfn|Żelazko|1965|loc=Theorem 13.17}} but there exist examples of non-commutative Fréchet <math>Q</math>-algebras which are not <math>m</math>-convex.{{sfn|Żelazko|1994|pp=283–290}}
* '''Properties of <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebras.''' A Fréchet algebra is <math>m</math>-convex if and only if it is a [[countable]] [[projective limit]] of Banach algebras.{{sfn|Michael|1952|loc=Theorem 5.1}} An element of <math>A</math> is invertible if and only if its image in each Banach algebra of the projective limit is invertible.{{efn|If <math>A</math> is non-unital, replace invertible with quasi-invertible.}}{{sfn|Michael|1952|loc=Theorem 5.2}}<ref>See also {{harvnb|Palmer|1994|loc=Theorem 2.9.6}}.</ref>

==Examples==
* '''Zero multiplication.''' If <math>E</math> is any Fréchet space, we can make a Fréchet algebra structure by setting <math>e * f = 0</math> for all <math>e, f \in E</math>.
* '''Smooth functions on the circle.''' Let <math>S^1</math> be the [[n-sphere|1-sphere]]. This is a 1-[[dimensional]] [[compact space|compact]] [[differentiable manifold]], with [[Manifold#Manifold with boundary|no boundary]]. Let <math>A=C^{\infty}(S^1)</math> be the set of [[Smoothness#Differentiability classes|infinitely differentiable]] complex-valued functions on <math>S^1</math>. This is clearly an algebra over the complex numbers, for [[pointwise#Pointwise operations|pointwise]] multiplication. (Use the [[product rule]] for [[derivative|differentiation]].) It is commutative, and the constant function <math>1</math> acts as an identity. Define a countable set of seminorms on <math>A</math> by <math display="block"> \left\| \varphi \right\|_{n} = \left \| \varphi^{(n)} \right \|_{\infty}, \qquad \varphi \in A, </math> where <math display="block"> \left \| \varphi^{(n)} \right \|_{\infty} = \sup_{x \in {S^1}} \left |\varphi^{(n)}(x) \right |</math> denotes the supremum of the absolute value of the <math>n</math>th derivative <math>\varphi^{(n)}</math>.{{efn|To see the completeness, let <math>\varphi_{k}</math> be a Cauchy sequence. Then each derivative <math>\varphi_{k}^{(l)}</math> is a Cauchy sequence in the sup norm on <math>S^1</math>, and hence converges uniformly to a continuous function <math>\psi_{l}</math> on <math>S^1</math>. It suffices to check that <math>\psi_{l}</math> is the <math>l</math>th derivative of <math>\psi_{0}</math>. But, using the [[fundamental theorem of calculus]], and taking the limit inside the integral (using [[uniform convergence]]), we have

:<math>\begin{align}
&{} \psi_{l}(x) - \psi_{l}(x_{0}) \\
= &{} \lim_{k \to \infty}\left ( \varphi_{k}^{(l)}(x) - \varphi_{k}^{(l)}(x_{0})\right) \\
= &{} \lim_{k \to\infty} \int_{x_{0}}^{x} \varphi_{k}^{(l+1)}(t) dt \\
= &{} \int_{x_{0}}^{x} \psi_{l+1}(t) dt.
\end{align}</math>}} Then, by the product rule for differentiation, we have <math display="block">\begin{align}
\| \varphi \psi \|_{n} &= \left \| \sum_{i = 0}^{n} {n \choose i} \varphi^{(i)} \psi^{(n-i)} \right \|_{\infty} \\
&\leq \sum_{i=0}^{n} {n \choose i} \| \varphi \|_{i} \| \psi \|_{n-i} \\
&\leq \sum_{i=0}^{n} {n \choose i} \| \varphi \|'_{n} \| \psi \|'_{n} \\
&=    2^n\| \varphi \|'_{n} \| \psi \|'_{n},
\end{align}</math> where <math display="block">{n \choose i} = \frac{n!}{{i! (n-i)!}},</math> denotes the [[binomial coefficient]] and <math display="block">\| \cdot \|'_{n} = \max_{k \leq n} \| \cdot \|_{k}.</math> The primed seminorms are submultiplicative after re-scaling by <math>C_n=2^n</math>.
* '''Sequences on <math>\N</math>.''' Let <math>\Complex^\N</math> be the [[sequence space|space of complex-valued sequences]] on the [[natural number]]s <math>\N</math>. Define an increasing family of seminorms on <math>\Complex^\N</math> by <math display="block">\| \varphi \|_n = \max_{k\leq n} |\varphi(k)|.</math> With pointwise multiplication, <math>\Complex^\N</math> is a commutative Fréchet algebra. In fact, each seminorm is submultiplicative <math> \| \varphi \psi \|_n \leq \| \varphi \|_n \| \psi \|_n</math> for <math> \varphi, \psi \in A </math>. This <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebra is unital, since the constant sequence <math>1(k) = 1, k \in \N</math> is in <math>A</math>.
* Equipped with the topology of [[uniform convergence]] on [[compact convergence|compact sets]], and pointwise multiplication, <math>C(\Complex)</math>, the algebra of all [[continuous function]]s on the [[complex plane]] <math>\Complex</math>, or to the algebra <math>\mathrm{Hol}(\Complex)</math> of [[holomorphic function]]s on <math>\Complex</math>.
* '''[[Convolution algebra]] of [[Vanish at infinity#Rapidly decreasing|rapidly vanishing functions]] on a finitely generated discrete group.''' Let <math>G</math> be a [[finitely generated group]], with the [[discrete topology]]. This means that there exists a set of finitely many elements <math>U= \{ g_{1}, \dots, g_{n}\} \subseteq G</math> such that: <math display="block">\bigcup_{n=0}^{\infty} U^n = G.</math> Without loss of generality, we may also assume that the identity element <math>e</math> of <math>G</math> is contained in <math>U</math>. Define a function <math>\ell : G \to [0, \infty)</math> by <math display="block">\ell(g) = \min \{ n \mid g \in U^n \}.</math> Then <math>\ell(gh ) \leq \ell(g) + \ell(h)</math>, and <math>\ell(e) = 0</math>, since we define <math>U^{0} = \{ e \}</math>.{{efn|

We can replace the generating set <math>U</math> with <math>U \cup U^{-1}</math>, so that <math>U=U^{-1}</math>. Then <math>\ell</math> satisfies the additional property <math>\ell(g^{-1})=\ell(g)</math>, and is a [[length function]] on <math>G</math>.}} Let <math>A</math> be the <math>\Complex</math>-vector space <math display="block">S(G) = \biggr\{ \varphi : G \to \Complex \,\,\biggl|\,\, \| \varphi \|_{d} < \infty,\quad d = 0,1, 2, \dots \biggr\},</math> where the seminorms <math>\| \cdot \|_{d}</math> are defined by <math display="block">\| \varphi \|_{d} = \| \ell^d \varphi \|_{1} =\sum_{g \in G} \ell(g)^d |\varphi(g)|.</math>{{efn|
To see that <math>A</math> is Fréchet space, let <math>\varphi_{n}</math> be a Cauchy sequence. Then for each <math>g \in G</math>, <math>\varphi_{n}(g)</math> is a Cauchy sequence in <math>\Complex</math>. Define <math>\varphi(g)</math> to be the limit. Then
:<math>\begin{align}
&\sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{n}(g) - \varphi(g)| \\
& \leq \sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{n}(g) - \varphi_{m}(g)|+ \sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{m}(g) - \varphi(g) | \\
& \leq \| \varphi_n - \varphi_m \|_d + \sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d |\varphi_{m}(g) - \varphi(g) |,
\end{align}</math>
where the sum ranges over any finite subset <math>S</math> of <math>G</math>. Let <math>\epsilon >0</math>, and let <math>K_{\epsilon}> 0</math> be such that <math>\| \varphi_n - \varphi_m \|_{d} < \epsilon</math> for <math>m, n \geq K_{\epsilon}</math>. By letting <math>m</math> run, we have
:<math>\sum_{g \in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{n}(g) - \varphi(g)| < \epsilon</math>
for <math>n \geq K_{\epsilon}</math>. Summing over all of <math>G</math>, we therefore have <math>\left\| \varphi_n - \varphi \right\|_d < \epsilon</math> for <math>n \geq K_{\epsilon}</math>. By the estimate
:<math>\begin{align}
&{}\sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi(g) | \\
&{} \leq \sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{n}(g) - \varphi(g)|+ \sum_{g\in S} \ell(g)^d | \varphi_{n}(g) | \\
&{} \leq \| \varphi_n - \varphi\|_d + \| \varphi_n \|_{d},
\end{align}</math>
we obtain <math>\| \varphi \|_{d} < \infty</math>. Since this holds for each <math>d \in \N</math>, we have <math>\varphi \in A</math> and <math>\varphi_n \to \varphi</math> in the Fréchet topology, so <math>A</math> is complete.}} <math>A</math> is an <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebra for the [[convolution#Convolutions on groups|convolution]] multiplication <math display="block">\varphi * \psi (g) = \sum_{h \in G} \varphi(h) \psi(h^{-1}g),</math>{{efn|
:<math>\begin{align}
& \| \varphi * \psi \|_{d} \\
& \leq \sum_{g \in G}\left ( \sum_{h \in G} \ell(g)^d |\varphi(h)| \left| \psi(h^{-1}g) \right| \right ) \\
&\leq \sum_{g, h \in G} \left (\ell(h) + \ell \left (h^{-1}g \right ) \right )^d |\varphi(h)| \left| \psi(h^{-1}g)\right| \\
&=  \sum_{i=0}^{d} {d \choose i} \left (\sum_{g, h \in G} \left |\ell^i \varphi(h) \right | \left |\ell^{d-i} \psi(h^{-1}g) \right | \right ) \\
&=  \sum_{i=0}^{d} {d \choose i} \left (\sum_{h \in G} \left |\ell^i \varphi(h) \right |\right)\left ( \sum_{g\in G} \left |\ell^{d-i} \psi(g) \right | \right) \\
&=  \sum_{i=0}^{d} {d \choose i} \| \varphi \|_{i} \| \psi \|_{d-i} \\
&\leq  2^d \| \varphi \|'_{d} \| \psi \|'_{d}
\end{align}</math>}} <math>A</math> is unital because <math>G</math> is discrete, and <math>A</math> is commutative if and only if <math>G</math> is [[Abelian group|Abelian]].
* '''Non <math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebras.''' The Aren's algebra <math display="block">A = L^\omega[0,1] = \bigcap_{p \geq 1} L^p[0,1]</math> is an example of a commutative non-<math>m</math>-convex Fréchet algebra with discontinuous inversion. The topology is given by [[L^p space|<math>L^p</math> norms]] <math display="block">\| f \|_p = \left ( \int_0^1 | f(t) |^p dt \right )^{1 / p}, \qquad f \in A,</math> and multiplication is given by [[convolution#Domain of definition|convolution]] of functions with respect to [[Lebesgue measure]] on <math>[0,1]</math>.{{sfn|Fragoulopoulou|2005|loc=Example 6.13 (2)}}

==Generalizations==
We can drop the requirement for the algebra to be locally convex, but still a [[complete metric space]]. In this case, the underlying space may be called a Fréchet space{{sfn|Waelbroeck|1971}} or an [[F-space]].{{sfn|Rudin|1973|loc=1.8(e)}}

If the requirement that the number of seminorms be countable is dropped, the algebra becomes locally convex (LC) or locally multiplicatively convex (LMC).{{sfnm|Michael|1952|Husain|1991}} A complete LMC algebra is called an Arens-Michael algebra.{{sfn|Fragoulopoulou|2005|loc=Chapter 1}}

==Michael's Conjecture==
The question of whether all linear multiplicative functionals on an <math>m</math>-convex Frechet algebra are continuous is known as Michael's Conjecture.<ref>{{harvnb|Michael|1952|loc=<math>\S</math> 12, Question 1}}; {{harvnb|Palmer|1994|loc=<math>\S</math> 3.1}}</ref> This conjecture is perhaps the most famous [[open problem]] in the theory of topological algebras.
